thread.title: Stocks poised to retreat slightly as crucial midterm elections get under way - MarketWatch

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Stocks poised to retreat slightly as crucial midterm elections get under way - MarketWatch
text:
U.S. stocks continued to edge higher midday Tuesday, as traders awaited the results of midterm elections that could set the political tone on Wall Street for at least the next two years.
How are the benchmarks performing? The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.68% rose 130 points, or 0.5%, to 25,593, the S&P 500 index SPX, +0.63% added 13 points to reach 2,751, a rise of 0.5%, and the Nasdaq Composite Index NQZ8, +0.92% climbed 0.7%, or 48 points, at 7,376.
On Monday, the Dow DJIA, +0.68% rose 190.87 points to 25,461.70, a gain of 0.8%, and the S&P 500 SPX, +0.63% added 15.25 points, or 0.6%, to end at 2,738.31. The Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, +0.64% meanwhile, fell 28.14 points, or 0.4%, to 7,328.85.
What’s driving the market? Midterm elections, which are expected to see Democrats take control of the House and Republicans maintain a grip on the Senate, are under way and the results could have implications for President Donald Trump’s legislative agenda.
Check out: How traders are thinking about dollar wagers ahead of midterm elections, the Fed
In the final pre-election Wall Street Journal/NBC News poll released Sunday, Democrats held a 7 percentage-point lead on the question of which party should control the next Congress.
The most likely outcome of the elections is political gridlock, which has historically been a positive for investors, but may forestall expectations for infrastructure investments and further deregulation that might help lift shares of financial firms.
Meanwhile, investors were keeping one eye on crude-oil prices CLZ8, -2.14% a day after the Trump administration imposed fresh sanctions aimed at curtailing Iranian oil exports.
Abroad, market participants are also watching developments around U.K. Prime Minister Theresa May and her tense negotiations with the European Union to exit a longstanding pact with the trade bloc.
Read : Opinion: This is what’s happened to stocks after every midterm election since World War II
Which stocks are in focus? Shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.08% were up 0.8%, a day after closing at their lowest level since Aug. 1 and booking the worst two-day decline since Jan. 25, 2013. Reports that the iPhone maker was scaling back on production of a new XR model phone had contributed to its decline.
Shares of Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +0.92% were in focus after reports that the retailing giant was set to pick two cities to host its second headquarters, possibly the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in New York and the Crystal City area of Arlington, Va., a Washington suburb. Shares of Amazon were up 1.4% Tuesday.
Under Armour Inc .’s UAA, -2.88% stock is down 3.2%, after a report in The Wall Street Journal. The company was in the spotlight after The Wall Street Journal reported it had banned the expensing of strip-club outings .
Shares of CVS Health Corp . CVS, +5.71% rose 4.7% after the firm announced 6.7% same-store sales growth for the third-quarter on Tuesday morning.
Eli Lilly & Co . LLY, -3.85% stock is down 3.8% after the pharmaceutical manufacturer reported third-quarter profit and revenue beats , and raised its full-year guidance for 2018. The stock is up 25% year-to-date.
E.l.f. Beauty Inc . shares have rallied 18.6% Tuesday, after its Monday-evening earnings report showed the cosmetics company producing third-quarter projections for revenue and profits that were better than expected. The firm also raised its full-year guidance for 2018.
Shares of Marriott International Inc . MAR, -5.08% tumbled 7% after the hotelier reported disappointing sales figures for the third quarter on Tuesday morning.
Mylan NV MYL, +16.13% stock is up more than 17%, after the pharmaceutical company announced Monday evening that its profits more than doubled in the third quarter from the year previous.
Shares of Avis Budget Group CAR, -4.90% are down 5% on the day, following a Monday evening earnings report that had the rental-car company falling short of analysts expectations for third-quarter sales and earnings.
Booking Holdings Inc . BKNG, +4.19% stock is up 5% Tuesday after the Priceline.com parent reported that it beat analysts estimates for sales and profi t in the third quarter.
Mosaic Company MOS, +10.61% shares are advancing 8%, following a third-quarter earnings report that showed the company benefiting from rising fertilizer prices .
Archer Daniels Midland Co . ADM, -1.60% stock is up 0.3% after food processing and commodities trading firm reported better-than-expected, third-quarter sales and earnings Tuesday morning. The stock is up 20.4% on the year.
Shares of Ralph Lauren Corp . RL, -6.59% were off 7.5%, even as the retailer reported revenue and profit beats for the third quarter on Tuesday morning . The stock is up 23.8% year-to-date.

What data are in focus The Labor Department reported that there were 7 million job openings in the U.S. in September, down from a record high 7.3 million in August. The number exceeds the 6.1 million Americans officially classified as unemployed.
What are analysts saying? Charlie Ripley, senior market strategist at Allianz Investment Management, said investors are predicting the Democrats to take the House of Representatives while the Republicans will retain control of the house. “We could see a lot more volatility in markets tonight and tomorrow if the result isn’t straight down the fairway,” he told MarketWatch.
If Democrats are able to overcome a deficit in the polls and take the Senate, that could create greater uncertainty, and set up potentially destabilizing political fights over White House oversight and the approval of executive and judicial branch appointments, Ripley said. “If we see the Republicans hang on to the house, that could be a boost to markets,” as this result could potentially lead to more aggressive deregulation and tax cuts, he said.
How are other markets trading? Asian markets were mixed Tuesday . European stocks were trading down on Monday, with the Stoxx Europe 600 SXXP, -0.26% falling 0.3%.
Oil prices CLZ8, -2.14% were slightly lower, while gold GCZ8, -0.37% was flat. The dollar DXY, -0.06% was virtually unchanged.
